Measles is a nationally notifiable disease in the US; CDC maintains an authoritative running case count — treat this as the primary reference for national totals.
CDC case counts are updated periodically (not daily); always record the 'as of' date associated with any CDC tally.
State health department reports may use different case definitions than CDC — note any definitional discrepancies in evidence_quote.
Q1 2025 (Jan–Mar) is a high-risk period for measles importation due to international travel; expect imported case flags in reports.
Outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities (religious exemption clusters, close-knit communities) are historically common in US measles epidemiology — prioritize subnational and locality fields.
Do not conflate measles outbreak case counts with national cumulative totals — record separately with appropriate scope.
Evidence quotes must be verbatim from source; do not paraphrase clinical or epidemiological figures.
If a source reports only 'X cases this week,' clarify whether this is incident or cumulative before populating case count fields.
Peer-reviewed literature for Q1 2025 events may not be available within the collection window — prioritize official agency and situation reports for this time period.

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment:
Coverage across the target fields is strong for the primary outbreak (Southwest US / West Texas Mennonite community):

• disease: Confirmed — Measles, across all accepted sources.
• country: United States — confirmed across all sources.
• subnational_location: Texas (primary), New Mexico (Lea County death confirmed via ArcGIS snippet and nmhealth.org), Oklahoma (OSDH March 11 link via MSK library guide), Kansas (coronavirus.kdheks.gov appeared in iteration 2 domain counts). Maryland (Howard County) also surfaced.
• locality: Gaines County TX, Lubbock TX, West Texas (Mennonite community), Lea County NM, Harris/Houston TX, Rockwall TX, Travis TX, Howard County MD — all identified from snippets.
• date_reported: Multiple Q1 2025 dates captured: January 2025 onset (Wikipedia, MSK guide), February 26 (first TX death — DSHS news release referenced in DSHS snippet, YouTube KSAT12 video, abc7ny.com), March 4 (Lubbock Online — 159 TX cases), March 6 (NM Lea County death — ArcGIS snippet), March 7 (CDC HAN advisory — 208 TX+NM cases), March 21 (Lubbock child care facility index case — MMWR mm7521a1).
• cases_confirmed: 124 (as of ~Feb 26, DSHS via abc7ny), 159 TX / Gaines County >100 (March 4, Lubbock Online), 208 TX+NM (March 7, CDC HAN), 800 total Jan 1–Apr 17 (MMWR mm7414a1 — partially outside Q1 window but Q1 sub-period data extractable), 505 TX (PBS — post-Q1), 750 TX final (Texas Tribune — post-Q1, useful for context only).
• deaths: 3 total confirmed — 2 children in Lubbock (first death Feb 26 per DSHS/abc7ny/YouTube; second death April 6 per DSHS snippet — outside Q1 window), 1 adult in Lea County NM (March 6 per ArcGIS snippet). Within strict Q1 window: at minimum 1 confirmed death (Feb 26 TX child) and 1 confirmed death (March 6 NM adult) = 2 deaths within Q1.
• hospitalizations: 18 hospitalized as of ~Feb 26 (DSHS via abc7ny); 85 hospitalized Jan 1–Apr 17 (MMWR mm7414a1 — partially outside Q1); >99 total (Wikipedia — full outbreak). Q1-specific hospitalization sub-totals will need annotation.
• source_url: Multiple authoritative URLs captured across cdc.gov (HAN, MMWR ×2, data page, global page), dshs.texas.gov, nmhealth.org, lubbockonline.com, texastribune.org, abc7ny.com, pbs.org, cidrap.umn.edu, publichealth.jhu.edu, paho.org (×4), who.int, en.wikipedia.org, libguides.mskcc.org, arcgis.com, reuters.com, nytimes.com, coronavirus.kdheks.gov.
• source_type: official_public_health_agency (CDC, DSHS, NMDOH, KDHE), international_organization_report (PAHO, WHO), news_and_situation_report (CIDRAP, Texas Tribune, Lubbock Online, PBS, abc7ny, Reuters, NYT), academic/tracker (JHU IVAC, Wikipedia).
• evidence_quote: Multiple extractable quotes from snippets (CDC HAN advisory text, MMWR aggregate text, abc7ny DSHS press release quote, Lubbock Online case count, ArcGIS NM death date).
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment:
High overall trustworthiness:
• CDC sources (cdc.gov) are the gold standard for US measles surveillance — HAN advisory and MMWR reports are peer-reviewed or officially cleared.
• Texas DSHS (dshs.texas.gov) is the primary state authority — press releases referenced in snippets are authoritative for TX-specific case counts and deaths.
• New Mexico DOH (nmhealth.org) is the primary state authority for NM data — the 2025 Measles Outbreak sub-page is present in the candidate set.
• PAHO (paho.org, 4 results) provides independent international validation.
• CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a highly regarded academic public health news outlet that consistently cites CDC as its primary source — suitable as a secondary corroborator.
• Texas Tribune (texastribune.org) explicitly states it used DSHS data from January–June 2025 — high credibility for TX-specific figures.
• Lubbock Online (lubbockonline.com) is a local outlet with direct access to Lubbock Public Health — suitable for locality-level detail.
• Wikipedia is useful for narrative and locality identification but numeric fields must be traced to primary sources.
• ArcGIS dashboard (arcgis.com) — the NM Lea County death snippet (3/6/25) is useful but the dashboard is a secondary aggregator; the nmhealth.org page is the preferred primary source for NM data.
• YouTube videos cannot yield evidence_quote extractions and should be deprioritized.
• Facebook result should be excluded as non-authoritative.
